chunks: From him, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya Al-Halabi, from Abdul-Hamid Al-Ta'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) looked at a man who had worn a shirt that touched the ground, so he said: 'Is this not a clean garment?'

key_terms.يُصِيبُ الْأَرْضَ: touching or dragging on the ground

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dragging one's garment on the ground in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) critiques *isbal* (dragging garments) not merely as a matter of vanity, but by questioning the ritual purity (*taharah*) of the fabric itself, implying that contact with the ground compromises its cleanliness. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the interplay between external appearance and internal spiritual state, where modesty in dress is intrinsically linked to the physical and metaphysical purity required for worship. The narration underscores the practical application of *taharah* in daily attire, reinforcing the Prophet's tradition of keeping garments free from dirt and impurity.

en.hubeali: From him, from his father, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Yahya Al Halby, from Abdul Hameed Al Ta’aiy, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> looked at a man who had worn a shirt which had been hitting the ground, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘These are not clean clothes’.
en.sarwar: 11. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya al-Halabiy from ‘Abd al-Hamid al-Ta’iy from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has narrated the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, looked at a man who had dressed in a shirt that dragged on the ground. He (the Imam) said, ‘This cloth is not clean.’”
